anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
OEConnection, LLC (**OEConnection**), through its wholly owned subsidiary, proposes to acquire 100% of the share capital of Quadrum Investments Group Ltd and its controlled subsidiaries (trading as **Epyx**) (the **Acquisition**).

OEConnection is a United States-based company that supplies software solutions for the automotive aftersales ecosystem, connecting suppliers, repairers, manufacturers and insurers through a spare parts marketplace, repair insights and supply chain solutions. OEConnection primarily supplies software and data solutions that facilitate the sale, sourcing and supply of automotive parts for vehicle repairs.

OEConnection is a controlled portfolio company of funds managed/advised by an affiliate of Francisco Partners Management, L.P. (**Francisco Partners**). Francisco Partners is a global private equity investment firm headquartered in the United States that primarily invests in technology and technology-enabled service businesses.

Epyx is a fleet technology solutions company headquartered in the United Kingdom that supplies fleet management software. Epyx’s primary offering is a fleet service, maintenance and repair authorisation platform called 1link Service Network. It connects vehicle fleet operators (such as leasing and rental companies) with automotive service providers (repair shops and garages), streamlining fleet service, maintenance and repair transactions. Epyx is indirectly owned by Corpay, Inc (NYSE: CPAY), a United States-based corporate payments and spend management company.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There is no material overlap between the services supplied by
OEConnection (or any connected entity of OEConnection) and
Epyx in Australia, given their different use cases and customer
bases. In particular, OEConnection’s services are primarily
supplied to original equipment manufacturers, whereas Epyx’s
service, maintenance and repair authorisation platform is
primarily supplied to fleet companies.
• OEConnection and Epyx each have a limited presence in
Australia.
